name: Middle Belt communal and herder-farmer violence (Plateau, Benue, southern Kaduna)
started: 2025-04-01 (2025-26 escalation in Plateau and Benue; conflict dates back decades)
summary: Raids on villages in Plateau, Benue and southern Kaduna, usually attributed to armed Fulani herders, and reprisals by farming-community militias continue to kill dozens at a time. ACLED recorded a 70%+ rise in Plateau's political violence in 2025 and its highest monthly level ever in April 2026. The violence is at the centre of US claims about persecution of Christians, which monitoring groups dispute.

sides.name: Farming-community militias and state forces
members: Operation Rainbow (Plateau state militia; about 1,400 recruits added end 2025)
leaders: State governments of Plateau and Benue
sides.strength: Operation Rainbow added about 1,400 fighters at end 2025 (ACLED).

background: The Middle Belt is where Nigeria's mostly Muslim north meets the mostly Christian south and where cattle routes cross expanding farmland. Land pressure, climate stress, the collapse of grazing reserves and weak policing have turned disputes into cycles of massacre and reprisal, mixed with banditry and kidnapping.

Why it matters: religious framing of the killings drove the US to designate Nigeria a 'country of particular concern' in late 2025 and fed the Christmas strikes debate, while ACLED and other monitors find that both Christians and Muslims are victims and that most jihadist victims in the northeast are Muslim.
year: Attacks continued through the window: at least 12 killed at a Plateau mining site (16 Dec 2025); about 20 killed in an ambush on security forces at Kanam, Plateau (13 Mar 2026); 30 killed in Jos North on 29 Mar (ACLED cites 33 in a Palm Sunday Jos attack); at least 20 killed over several hours in Kwatas ward, Bokkos (9 Apr) with no security response; 20 at Kawel, Bokkos (21 Jun); and attacks around Otukpo in Benue (13 and 28 Jul, 8 and 14 killed) and Naridon, Kauru, Kaduna (27 Jul, 30 killed). April 2026 recorded the most political violence incidents in Plateau since ACLED coverage began in 1997, almost 60% of them attacks on civilians. Nine people were charged in Feb 2026 for a 2025 massacre that killed 150.
situation: As of late October 2026 violence remains endemic in Plateau's Bokkos, Bassa, Mangu and Jos areas, Benue's Otukpo and Guma areas and southern Kaduna, with state-backed militias growing and federal forces stretched. No overarching peace process exists.
technical: Attack pattern: night raids by armed groups on motorcycles on isolated villages, lasting hours, often without security response (ACLED on Kwatas, Bokkos, 9 Apr 2026).
Attacks on civilians made up almost 60% of violent incidents in Plateau in April 2026 (ACLED).
Plateau's political violence rose more than 70% in 2025 compared with 2024 (ACLED).
State responses lean on militias: Plateau recruited about 1,400 fighters for Operation Rainbow at end 2025 (ACLED).
Benue's Otukpo-Makurdi highway is a kidnapping corridor (bus passengers abducted 16 Apr 2026).
Ambushes on security forces also occur, e.g. Kanam, Plateau, about 20 killed (13 Mar 2026).

Religious framing is contested: ACLED says most victims of jihadist violence in the northeast are Muslims, and monitors find no evidence that Christians are killed more than Muslims nationally (as reported by the BBC and ACLED).
casualties: No consolidated 12-month toll found. Listed incidents in the sources total several hundred deaths (Plateau, Benue, southern Kaduna), and ACLED reports record levels in Plateau in April 2026. The 'high' rating is an estimate based on these trends and is uncertain.

timeline.event: Attack on a Plateau mining site kills at least 12.
Ambush on security forces at Kanam, Plateau kills about 20.
30 killed in an attack in Jos North.
At least 20 killed in Kwatas ward, Bokkos; April becomes Plateau's most violent month on record.
At least 20 killed at Kawel, Bokkos.
At least 30 killed at Naridon, Kauru, Kaduna.

outlook: Watch the dry-season migration period (roughly November to April), when clashes typically rise, the growth of state militias, and how US religious-freedom pressure shapes Abuja's response.

zones.name: Plateau (Bokkos, Mangu, Bassa, Jos)
zones.note: Record violence in April 2026; Jos North, Kwatas and Kawel attacks.

zones.name: Benue (Otukpo, Guma, Makurdi)
zones.note: Village raids and highway kidnappings; Otukpo attacks July 2026.

zones.name: Southern Kaduna (Kauru, Kajuru)
zones.note: Naridon attack (30 killed) July 2026; church abductions.
